content_sections.body_text: Use was/were + verb-ing for an action already in progress: ‘I was running home when it began to rain.’ Here run means move on foot faster than walking. Draw a long line for was running and a point for the moment it began to rain.
content_sections.title: Retrieve scene and movement

content_sections.body_text: Mai: ‘I was running home when it began to rain. Please help me carry these books.’ An: ‘Of course. I’ll carry the books in my bag.’ Mai: ‘Thank you.’ Mai states what must be carried; An explicitly agrees to carry it, so the response solves the request.
content_sections.title: Connect request and response

content_sections.body_text: Retell in order: ‘First, Mai was running home. Then it began to rain. Next, she requested help. Finally, An carried the books.’ Say ‘An carried the BOOKS, not the umbrella’ to focus BOOKS; say ‘AN carried the books, not Mai’ to focus AN. The contrast determines the prominent word.
content_sections.title: Sequence and focus the account

content_sections.body_text: Create a new four-part account: ongoing movement, a natural weather change, a clear carrying request, and a reply that names what the helper will carry. Record it. Check: run keeps its foot-movement sense, the order is clear, the helper explicitly carries the requested item, and prominence matches one stated contrast.
